recommendation: Keep the fix as-is. If a future global concept-search or cross-CodeSystem facility is desired, it should be introduced by a new work-group decision rather than by preserving the old @all redirect.
issue_request: FHIR-19442 was Published and resolved Not Persuasive with Modification for R5. It asked about moving the terminology-service section "Operations across all value sets" and whether @all should instead be defined as an operation; the final resolution was to remove the section because the feature was limited, server-specific, and not interoperable.
initial_application: The R5 vocab batch commit 9500b398d1 removed the @all narrative section and anchor from source/terminology-service.html. Current terminology-service.html remains correct, but publish.ini still had a current [redirects] entry defining http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/@all as a "Magic ValueSet Id" pointing to the deleted terminology-service.html#all anchor.
additional_context: source/terminology-service.html is active through the current hierarchy and documentation pages, and publish.ini is the checked-in top-level publishing configuration rather than generated publish/ output. Vocab minutes and Jira comments confirm the work group chose removal from core while allowing custom terminology server behavior. Later Zulip discussion says @all is no longer defined in R5+ and was an internal construct that should not have been externally visible.
reconciliation: Removed the stale http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/@all redirect from publish.ini so current publication metadata no longer exposes a core-defined magic ValueSet URL for the removed section.
source_changes: publish.ini: removed the http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/@all redirect from the [redirects] section.
